To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The use of multiplanar MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) for the detection of prostate cancer (PCa) and its local extension, as well as for the staging of the seminal vesicles (SVs) and the regional lymph nodes (LNs), is a valuable tool in the management of PCa.

the addition of multiplanar (axial, sagittal and coronal) cross-referencing of the prostate gland to endorectal MR imaging (MRI) for the staging of patients with newly diagnosed clinically localized prostate cancer provides incremental value in the assessment of extraprostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion.
multiplanar cross-reference (MPCR) is a useful tool for prostate cancer staging, especially when the prostate gland is not completely visible in the axial plane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for prostate cancer staging using endorectal MRI (endorectal MRI) and the evaluation of this method in a prospective clinical trial.
the use of a multiplanar cross-reference (MPCR) technique for prostate cancer staging using endorectal MRI (ER-MRI) and the incremental value of MPCR over conventional ER-MRI.
the development of a new approach to the problem of prostate cancer staging using multiplanar crossreferencing with endorectal MR images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MRI is a useful tool for staging prostate cancer.
the evidence is not sufficient to recommend routine use of MRI for the staging of patients with prostate cancer.
the current evidence does not support the use of endorectal coil in MRI prostate cancer staging and that the routine use of endoreactal coil is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our research is focused on the development of new technologies to enable the detection and diagnosis of cancer, and the treatment and prevention of cancer.
multiplanar cross-sectional imaging with T2-weighted MRI of the prostate provides the highest accuracy for staging clinically localized prostate cancer.
the incremental value of multiplananr cross-referencing (MCR) for prostate cancer staging is limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the incremental value of multiplanal cross-referencing is limited in the staging of prostate cancer with endorectal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in the setting of a negative digital rectal examination (DRE).
the addition of multiplanar MRI to the staging protocol can help identify additional areas of disease that would have been missed by conventional imaging alone.
the addition of multiplanar MRI cross-referencing to endorectal MRI improves prostate cancer staging by providing additional information regarding the extent and location of the disease.
